title: A Separation between Full-Rank PVM and Assumption-free Self-Testing
abstract: We construct a nonlocal game that self-tests a maximally entangled qubit strategy among pure full-Schmidt-rank projective strategies, but admits an inequivalent optimum using one nonprojective measurement. This resolves a conjecture of Baptista et al. on imposing full rank and projectivity simultaneously. The construction combines CHSH with an auxiliary game $G$ that forces deterministic answers under these assumptions and admits a trine POVM optimum without them. We classify the optimal correlations of $G$ as a line segment parametrized by the tracial states of $\mathbb{C}\oplus M_2(\mathbb{C})$. Projectivity on the state support removes the matrix summand, whereas projective dilations with nonzero nonabort probability have a nontracial local state whose zero left ideal is not two-sided. Finally, a family in local dimension six shows that the full-rank PVM self-test is not robust.
summary: This paper resolves a conjecture regarding the self-testing of entangled quantum strategies by constructing a nonlocal game $H$. It proves that restricting the measurements to pure, full-rank projective measurements (PVMs) is not robust, as a nonprojective measurement can achieve superior correlations. The work relies on detailed algebraic analysis of optimal correlation structures.
main_problem: The paper investigates the robustness of self-testing protocols for maximally entangled qubit strategies when restricting measurements to pure full-Schmidt-rank Projective Measurements (PVMs).
main_result: It proves that the full-rank PVM self-test is not robust because an optimal strategy using a nonprojective measurement can achieve correlations unattainable by any pure full-rank PVM strategy.
method: The authors construct a nonlocal game $H$ by combining the CHSH game with an auxiliary game $G$. They use algebraic classification of optimal correlations and the concept of local dilation to establish the separation.
model_or_system: The study uses a nonlocal game $H$ played on a shared maximally entangled qubit state $|\Phi^+angle$ on $\mathbb{C}^2 \otimes \mathbb{C}^2$. The analysis involves comparing correlations derived from PVMs versus those from general measurements.
key_observables: Quantum and classical values of the game $H$ ($\omega_q(H)$ vs $\omega_c(H)$), and the optimal correlation values for the auxiliary game $G$ ($19/22$).
important_parameters: The parameter $t \in (0, 1)$ controlling the deviation from a reference state $	ext{S}_0$, and the structure of the local state algebra (e.g., $\mathbb{C} \oplus M_2(\mathbb{C})$).
main_assumptions: The core assumption being tested is the simultaneous requirement of full rank and projectivity on the measurement effects. The analysis also uses the assumption of block-diagonal measurements for the abort/nonabort subspaces.
paper_structure: The paper first analyzes a simpler game $G$ to show that full-rank PVMs constrain the optimal correlations to a specific subset. It then combines $G$ with the CHSH game to construct $H$, demonstrating the separation between the PVM-restricted set and the general quantum set.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous, algebraic demonstration of the limitations of assuming measurement projectivity in quantum information tasks, which is crucial for understanding the fundamental boundaries of quantum correlations.
